court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: M. Muthuraj vs The Deputy General Of Police

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: M. Muthuraj — son of deceased Sub-Inspector of Police
parties.respondent_defendant: The Deputy General of Police, Tamil Nadu Police Department, Chennai and The Superintendent of Police, Tuticorin District

facts_of_case: Petitioner's father was a Sub-Inspector of Police who expired in an accident. Petitioner's mother is the second wife of his father. Petitioner seeks employment on compassionate grounds after rejection of representation by respondents.

legal_principles.principle: The law relating to compassionate appointment should be read in line with the provisions available in the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the law relating to compassionate appointment especially with reference to dependents, should be read in line with the provisions available in the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The Government has the power to make policies that restrict Fundamental Rights and Personal Law in the larger public interest.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, certain restrictions on Fundamental Rights and Personal Law are made in Service rules in the larger public interest.
cited_cases: M. Muthuraj vs The Deputy General Of Police, (2016)

outcome.final_order: Court directs respondents to provide petitioner with employment on compassionate grounds and quashes impugned orders.

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India
seeking compassionate appointment in police department
challenging rejection of representation for compassionate appointment
